messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: spike in 5xxs and gateway timeouts for private-inference-gw-us-west-2. Alert threshold tripped at 09:12 UTC. Automated paging to oncall.
Emily (oncall): I'm on it, paging SRE and NetOps. Which tenants impacted?
Customer Success: Seeing multiple customer support tickets — two large customers report 504s when calling /v1/generate through private endpoint.
Sanjay: grabbing metrics now, looks like backend connectivity spikes and SYN retrans before 504s. 5xx rate jumped from 0.3% -> 8% starting ~09:10.
Matt: I see a surge in NAT translations on the transit appliance for the private VPC. Port exhaustion pattern? per-host ephemeral ports near limit.
Sara: Confirmed peering table shows repeated route target changes around 09:05 across a few AZs, likely a BGP flapping or config push.
Emily (oncall): Ok quick plan: 1) verify NAT ephemeral exhaustion 2) if confirmed, enable temporary egress via public-proxy for affected subnets 3) rollback recent SG/route rollout if correlated. Assigning roles: Sanjay network debug, Matt mitigation (egress change), Sara customer comms.
Sanjay: running `netstat -an | grep tcp | wc -l` on transit appliance, lots of TIME_WAIT but also many ESTABLISHED to external model-hosts. Dumping conntrack:```sudo conntrack -L | tail -n 20
udp      17 29 src=10.12.5.21 dst=13.32.10.9 sport=48723 dport=443 packets=12 bytes=1024 [ASSURED] mark=0 use=1
tcp      6 431999 ESTABLISHED src=10.12.5.30 dst=35.182.44.12 sport=54122 dport=443 packets=450 bytes=51200 mark=0 use=2
...```
NetOps-Bot: NAT allocation percent for transit-appliance-1: 96% ephemeral ports used, forecast to hit 100% in ~7m at current rate.
Matt: I'm going to add temporary NAT pool expansion and enable short-lived port reuse to relieve pressure. Pushing commands to jumpbox:```aws ec2 allocate-address --domain vpc --tag-specifications 'ResourceType=elastic-ip,Tags=[{Key=incident,Value=3212345678}]'```
Emily (oncall): Before making egress change — any security/regulatory concerns for routing to public-proxy? Which customers are on these subnets?
Sara: Two regulated customers A and B are on affected VPCs — need approval for public egress. Customer Success is attempting to reach them.
Customer Success: Reaching out now, asking for consent to temporary failover to managed-proxy for 30m. We'll note this as incident mitigation.
Sanjay: Additional data: packet captures show asymmetric TTL and `DF` flags inconsistent — suggests a transit appliance NAT/masquerade mismatch after recent fw rollout. I suspect `DNAT` rule ordering changed earlier in the rollout.
Matt: I see a config push at 08:58 from `eng-rotation` that touched `fw-transit` rules. Rolling back that change might restore NAT behavior. Can we rollback one commit?
eng-rotation: That push touched rule IDs 7203/7204 (DNAT to model-inference pool). We can revert to commit `d4f9a2` but need approval.
Emily (oncall): Approve rollback if we can do it safely. Sanjay and Matt coordinate: rollback + NAT pool expansion simultaneously to buy time. Try to avoid public egress for regulated customers unless absolutely needed.
Sanjay: Rolling back DNAT order now:```sudo iptables-restore < /tmp/iptables-prev-2026-03-15```. Reordering complete. Applying conntrack flush for affected flows:```sudo conntrack -F -s 10.12.0.0/16```
Matt: NAT pool expansion applied, additional EIPs attached to transit appliance, ephemeral usage dropped to 64% per NetOps-Bot.
NetOps-Bot: NAT allocation percent for transit-appliance-1: 64% used. 5xx rate partially reduced to 3.2%. Latency for private-gw now improving.
Sara: Customer Success reports one of the regulated customers acknowledged and accepted temporary proxy failover just in case. They asked for rollback timeline and postmortem.
Customer Success: Noted — we'll coordinate a short CS update: ETA mitigation 15-25m, possible limited impact for some API calls.
Emily (oncall): Any sign of continued BGP flaps or peering instability? We should keep an eye on route table churn.
Sanjay: BGP adjacency stable now after rollback, no further route updates in last 4m. `show ip bgp neighbors` stable.
Matt: Doing a canary verification of inference requests via private gw -> model-host. `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED" https://private-gw-us-west-2/v1/generate -d '{"prompt":"test"}'` returned 200 and tokens streaming.
Sara: I'll prepare the customer-facing incident note and tag impacted tenants. Need exact start/end times once this is closed.
Emily (oncall): Good work. For follow-ups: - open a postmortem ticket, include the fw-transit rollout as root cause candidate - plan safer DNAT rule deployment (test ordering invariant) - increase NAT port pool or implement better port reuse heuristics for transit appliance - add alert for rapid conntrack growth.
eng-rotation: Creating postmortem ticket `INC-321234` and assigning to eng-networking + infra.
Customer Success: Sent preliminary status update to tenants. One asks if request retries contributed to exhaustion — likely yes, we'll include that in postmortem.
NetOps-Bot: Incident metrics: peak 5xx 8.4%, duration of elevated errors ~ 22m, impacted requests ~ 42k.
Emily (oncall): Closing paging for now, keep monitoring for 1h. If any reoccurrence, escalate to SEV2. :thumbsup:
incidents-bot: Incident resolved signal at 09:44 UTC. Incident channel will stay open for postmortem discussion.
